**Element Layout (13.5 points):**
The split-screen design effectively separates conceptual text from visual proofs. Spatial balance is maintained, though some mathematical formulas feel slightly crowded compared to the ample whitespace in text blocks.

**Attractiveness (12.8 points):**
The high-contrast dark theme and smooth vector animations create a professional aesthetic. Color coding for variables (rabbits/foxes) aids engagement, though the overall visual style is standard for mathematical content.

**Logic Flow (14.2 points):**
The progression is pedagogically sound, moving from a concrete population hook to Taylor series prerequisites, then to matrix definitions and geometric intuition. Scaffolding is handled with high clarity.

**Accuracy & Depth (14.5 points):**
The content is mathematically rigorous, accurately presenting the Taylor expansion for matrices and the diagonalization shortcut. It bridges the gap between algebraic definition and differential equation applications effectively.

**Visual Consistency (13.8 points):**
The video maintains a unified color palette and typographic style throughout. Transition timing between the left-hand bullet points and right-hand animations is synchronized and predictable.

**Overall Summary:**
This video provides a solid instructional framework for understanding matrix exponentials by blending algebraic rigor with geometric intuition. It follows a classic pedagogical structure that is well-suited for university-level linear algebra students.

**Key Strengths:**
• Effective use of Taylor series as a prerequisite bridge
• Clear geometric visualization of continuous flow
• Consistent use of color coding to link variables to graph lines

**Areas for Improvement:**
• Increase font size for complex matrix subscripts to improve readability
• Provide brief pauses between dense mathematical transitions for better cognitive processing
• Incorporate more varied layouts to reduce the repetitive nature of the split-screen

B
The matrix exponential provides the solution to systems of linear differential equations (dx/dt = Ax), which are essential for modeling the behavior of dynamic systems over time.

C
Raising a matrix to a power (A³) is defined as multiplying the matrix by itself that number of times using standard matrix multiplication, so A³ = A * A * A.

B
The formula for the matrix exponential e^{A} is defined by its Taylor series, which is the direct matrix analogue of the series for the scalar exponential e^x. The series is Σ (A^k / k!) for k=0 to infinity, which expands to I + A + A²/2! + A³/3! + ...

A
The matrix exponential e^D is defined by its Taylor series. For a diagonal matrix D, D^k is a diagonal matrix with entries (d_i)^k. The series then simplifies to applying the scalar exponential function to each diagonal entry independently.

C
This is the direct matrix analog of the solution to the scalar equation dx/dt = ax, which is x(t) = e^(at)x(0). The matrix exponential e^(At) is defined by its Taylor series expansion, and differentiating it term by term confirms it is the solution.
